product: IR Worldview Inventory - World Stage homepage scene ledger

editorialNotes.intendedUse: Educational editorial mapping, not live intelligence
editorialNotes.coordinatePolicy: Rounded public approximations for homepage cartography
editorialNotes.magnitudePolicy: No invented quantitative magnitudes; 1-3 values are editorial ordinal weights only

scenes.oneSentencePurpose: The Indo-Pacific treaty system links U.S. forward forces, host-nation infrastructure, and distributed deterrence.
scenes.evidenceWindow: asOf 2026-07-14; treaty texts remain in force, posture details use latest public material cited

countryRoles.rationale: This scene is organized around U.S. treaty commitments, forward posture, and budgeted resilience investments in the Indo-Pacific.
The 1960 Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security and Article VI basing arrangements make Japan a core host and treaty partner.
The 1953 Mutual Defense Treaty and the centrality of Camp Humphreys make South Korea a core treaty and posture node.
The 1951 Mutual Defense Treaty, Visiting Forces Agreement framework, and EDCA expansion place the Philippines inside the active alliance map.
ANZUS and the U.S. Force Posture Initiatives, especially Marine Rotational Force-Darwin and related infrastructure, make Australia a key alliance platform.
Official U.S.-India and Indian statements describe a comprehensive global strategic partnership. The relationship has no formal mutual-defense treaty.
U.S. ties are officially robust but unofficial, grounded in the Taiwan Relations Act rather than a defense treaty; Taiwan sits inside the lens as a contingency-shaping actor.
Recent U.S. Indo-Pacific posture documents explicitly prioritize deterrence against the PRC, making China the principal competitive reference point in this lens.

nodes.label: Washington, DC
nodes.whyItMatters: Washington sets U.S. treaty policy, defense budgets, and regional force posture.

nodes.label: Yokosuka
nodes.whyItMatters: Yokosuka hosts the U.S. 7th Fleet and the Navy's only permanently forward-deployed carrier strike group.

nodes.label: Kadena Air Base
nodes.whyItMatters: Kadena is a major U.S. air-power hub in the Pacific.

nodes.label: Camp Humphreys
nodes.whyItMatters: The largest overseas U.S. military installation anchors the Korean Peninsula portion of the alliance map.

nodes.label: Manila
nodes.whyItMatters: Manila manages alliance diplomacy, VFA and EDCA implementation, and maritime-security coordination.

nodes.label: Darwin
nodes.whyItMatters: Darwin hosts Marine Rotational Force-Darwin and sits inside the U.S. Force Posture Initiatives as a recurring alliance platform.

nodes.label: Andersen AFB and Joint Region Marianas
nodes.whyItMatters: Guam supports Indo-Pacific power projection and a more dispersed U.S. force posture.

nodes.label: Tokyo
nodes.whyItMatters: Tokyo decides host-nation support, force modernization, and the politics of the bilateral alliance.

flows.label: U.S.-Japan treaty and basing framework
flows.plain-language meaning: A mutual-security treaty and basing agreements make Japan a core host for U.S. forces.

flows.label: U.S.-ROK mutual defense and basing
flows.plain-language meaning: The U.S.-ROK treaty supports the continued stationing of U.S. land, air, and sea forces in South Korea.

flows.label: U.S.-Philippines MDT plus EDCA access
flows.plain-language meaning: The 1951 treaty and EDCA give U.S. forces access to Philippine sites and support joint operations.

flows.label: U.S. rotational posture through Darwin
flows.plain-language meaning: Darwin provides recurring rotational access. It does not have the status of a permanent treaty base like those in Japan or South Korea.

flows.label: Guam to forward alliance arc
flows.plain-language meaning: Guam and Japan form linked nodes in a dispersed U.S. forward network, though their legal authorities and missions differ.

caveats: Stale≤6mo: U.S. tactical-aircraft laydown, FY-budgeted posture projects, and EDCA implementation pace can change quickly.
A simplified homepage map may wrongly imply that all treaty partners offer identical legal authorities, domestic political consent, and military access; they do not.
Taiwan should not be colored or labeled as a formal treaty ally in this scene because the U.S. relationship is explicitly unofficial and law-based rather than treaty-based.
sensitiveOrDisputedClassifications: Taiwan classification is highly sensitive; 'exposed or dependent actor' is used here to avoid implying diplomatic recognition or a mutual-defense treaty.
Darwin is a rotational posture site under Australian control; mapping it like a permanent U.S. base would mislead.
missingEvidence: Public sources do not provide a single authoritative point-to-point map of legal access, command authorities, and contingency commitments across all alliance nodes.
Public budget and posture documents do not fully capture classified contingency planning.

scenes.oneSentencePurpose: Beijing's regional security map centers sovereignty disputes, nearby theaters, strategic partnerships, and selective overseas access.
scenes.evidenceWindow: asOf 2026-07-14; uses PRC official white papers, MFA statements, MOD briefings, and partner-government material

countryRoles.rationale: The scene is organized around PRC defense policy, sovereignty claims, regional consultation mechanisms, and security-partnership arrangements.
Official PRC statements define the relationship as a 'new-era comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination' and explicitly deny that it is a Cold War-style alliance.
China and Pakistan officially describe their relationship as an all-weather strategic cooperative partnership, with CPEC and Gwadar embedded in wider cooperation.
Cambodia's Ream modernization and joint logistics/training center materially pull Cambodia into the Beijing-centered security picture, even as Phnom Penh rejects claims of exclusivity.
China and the Philippines maintain a bilateral consultation mechanism on the South China Sea, but PRC official language simultaneously frames Philippine maritime actions as infringements.
PRC white papers and Eastern Theater statements treat Taiwan as a sovereignty issue and a core military-theater focus. They do not treat it as an external peer state.
PRC defense and security documents frame U.S.-led alliances and military activity as central adverse pressures in the regional environment.

nodes.label: Beijing
nodes.whyItMatters: Beijing sets the sovereignty claims, security concepts, and partnership labels that organize this view.

nodes.label: Eastern Theater command axis
nodes.whyItMatters: Eastern Theater Command directs cross-strait military pressure and signaling.

nodes.label: Zhanjiang
nodes.whyItMatters: Zhanjiang anchors Southern Theater Navy operations in the South China Sea.

nodes.label: Xiamen
nodes.whyItMatters: Xiamen hosted the 2025 China-Philippines Bilateral Consultation Mechanism meeting on the South China Sea.

nodes.label: Ream Naval Base
nodes.whyItMatters: Ream hosts a Cambodia-China joint logistics and training center.

nodes.label: Gwadar
nodes.whyItMatters: Gwadar links CPEC to the Arabian Sea and China's westward economic corridor.

nodes.label: Moscow
nodes.whyItMatters: Moscow is Beijing's highest-level strategic partner. The relationship has no formal alliance treaty.

nodes.label: Manila
nodes.whyItMatters: Manila is both a rival claimant and a formal dialogue partner.

flows.label: Beijing-Moscow strategic coordination
flows.plain-language meaning: China and Russia maintain a high-level strategic partnership without a mutual-defense treaty.

flows.label: Beijing-Gwadar CPEC corridor
flows.plain-language meaning: Gwadar connects CPEC to the Arabian Sea; it is not an acknowledged Chinese naval base.

flows.label: Beijing-Ream logistics and training link
flows.plain-language meaning: Ream hosts a Cambodia-China logistics and training center. Cambodia says the base is not exclusive to China.

flows.label: Xiamen-Manila South China Sea consultation channel
flows.plain-language meaning: The Xiamen-Manila consultation channel supports formal talks despite the South China Sea dispute.

caveats: Stale≤6mo: PRC military exercises around Taiwan, rhetoric in regular press briefings, and the public framing of Ream can shift quickly.

A simplified homepage map may wrongly imply that all PRC partnerships are equivalent; PRC-Russia, PRC-Pakistan, and PRC-Cambodia relationships differ in legal form, capability depth, and strategic purpose.
This lens depicts Beijing's view. Sovereignty claims remain disputed and are not presented as internationally settled facts.
sensitiveOrDisputedClassifications: Taiwan classification is highly sensitive; wording here reflects PRC official framing without endorsing it.
Ream Naval Base status is disputed; public evidence supports a joint logistics/training center, but exclusivity and wartime-use assumptions remain contested in open sources.
missingEvidence: Public sources do not reveal confidential military understandings, actual contingency permissions, or operational access terms at Ream or Gwadar.
Open-source PRC materials identify theaters and partnerships more readily than detailed command-and-control arrangements.

scenes.oneSentencePurpose: These states preserve autonomy through selective engagement and issue-based coalitions while avoiding fixed bloc membership.
scenes.lensOwner: No single owner; editorially centered on autonomous middle-power statecraft
scenes.evidenceWindow: asOf 2026-07-14; uses official foreign-policy doctrines and summit materials

countryRoles.rationale: Indian official statements continue to foreground strategic autonomy and a comprehensive but non-allied pattern of major-power engagement.
Indonesia's official 'bebas aktif' doctrine explicitly rejects alignment with superpowers while insisting on active diplomacy.
Vietnamese official diplomacy describes an independent, self-reliant, diversified, and multilateralized approach often summarized as 'bamboo diplomacy.'
Brazil's 2025 BRICS presidency and summit-hosting role show an effort to shape multipolar governance without reducing foreign policy to a single camp.
Saudi official documents show simultaneous pursuit of a comprehensive strategic partnership with China and ongoing strategic dealings with the United States.
The UAE's official foreign-policy principles stress non-interference and broad external partnerships, while its economic and technology ties span multiple major powers.

nodes.label: New Delhi
nodes.whyItMatters: New Delhi pursues strategic autonomy across competing relationships.

nodes.label: Jakarta
nodes.whyItMatters: Jakarta anchors Indonesia's bebas aktif doctrine and its ASEAN diplomacy.

nodes.label: ASEAN Secretariat
nodes.whyItMatters: The ASEAN Secretariat coordinates the bloc's consensus-based, nonaligned diplomacy.

nodes.label: Hanoi
nodes.whyItMatters: Hanoi directs Vietnam's diversified, self-reliant foreign policy.

nodes.label: Brasília
nodes.whyItMatters: Brasília directs Brazil's BRICS diplomacy and global-governance agenda.

nodes.label: Rio de Janeiro
nodes.whyItMatters: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2025 BRICS summit.

nodes.label: Riyadh
nodes.whyItMatters: Energy, investment, and summit diplomacy let Riyadh keep channels open with multiple great powers.

nodes.label: Abu Dhabi
nodes.whyItMatters: Abu Dhabi uses capital, technology ties, and diplomacy to hedge across major powers.

caveats: Stale≤6mo: summit calendars, rotating presidencies, and transactional openings can shift fast and should not be treated as fixed structural alignments.

A simplified homepage map may overstate coherence among 'hedgers'; India's autonomy, Indonesia's bebas aktif, Vietnam's bamboo diplomacy, Brazil's governance entrepreneurship, and Gulf multi-vector diplomacy are not the same strategy.
This scene is intentionally thinner on militarized flows because it examines how states preserve choice across several relationships. A single institutionalized network would misstate that pattern.
sensitiveOrDisputedClassifications: Saudi and Emirati roles are best treated as hedging rather than as stable attachment to any single external pole.
Brazil's BRICS role can be politicized domestically and internationally; the ledger treats it as governance positioning, not camp membership.
missingEvidence: No single official dataset measures 'hedging'; this scene rests on doctrine texts, summit roles, and official partnership language rather than a quantified index.
Open sources often understate how much domestic politics shape middle-power room for maneuver.

scenes.oneSentencePurpose: Chip production is a cross-border network with bottlenecks at different stages and in different countries.
scenes.evidenceWindow: asOf 2026-08-02; uses company annual reports, official factory pages, and government industrial-policy material

countryRoles.rationale: Taiwan hosts multiple TSMC leading-edge fab nodes that remain central to global foundry production and overseas network expansion.
South Korea remains central through Samsung's large-scale memory and foundry manufacturing base anchored at Pyeongtaek.
The United States combines design and policy power with TSMC's Arizona expansion and major equipment-company headquarters and production capacity.
The Netherlands is both a bottleneck supplier location through ASML and a policy chokepoint through export controls on advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
Japan combines state-backed fab expansion with globally important equipment, silicon-wafer, and photoresist production sites.
Malaysia's official semiconductor strategy and major Penang packaging/test expansions place it inside higher-value backend and ecosystem roles.
ZEISS produces the advanced lithography optics integrated into ASML systems, making Oberkochen a distinct upstream equipment chokepoint.

nodes.label: Hsinchu Science Park
nodes.whyItMatters: Hsinchu concentrates Taiwan's semiconductor foundries and research.

nodes.label: TSMC Fab 18, Tainan
nodes.whyItMatters: Fab 18 is a flagship advanced-node manufacturing complex.

nodes.label: TSMC Arizona, Phoenix
nodes.whyItMatters: TSMC's Phoenix fabs extend Taiwan-centered foundry production into the United States.

nodes.label: Pyeongtaek Campus
nodes.whyItMatters: Pyeongtaek is Samsung's largest semiconductor production complex for memory and foundry manufacturing.

nodes.label: ASML Veldhoven
nodes.whyItMatters: ASML's largest research and manufacturing site makes Veldhoven a bottleneck for advanced lithography.

nodes.label: JASM Kumamoto
nodes.whyItMatters: The TSMC-linked Kumamoto fab anchors Japan's semiconductor revival.

nodes.label: Penang packaging and test cluster
nodes.whyItMatters: Penang is a major center for semiconductor packaging and testing.

nodes.label: Tokyo Electron Yamanashi (Fujii)
nodes.whyItMatters: Tokyo Electron develops and manufactures deposition, etch, coater/developer, and related semiconductor production equipment in its Yamanashi network.

nodes.label: Applied Materials, Santa Clara
nodes.whyItMatters: Santa Clara is Applied Materials' headquarters; its U.S. manufacturing footprint supplies systems used across semiconductor fabrication.

nodes.label: Lam Research, Fremont
nodes.whyItMatters: Fremont anchors Lam Research's headquarters and a separately listed manufacturing site for wafer-fabrication equipment.

nodes.label: KLA, Milpitas
nodes.whyItMatters: KLA's Milpitas base anchors process-control, inspection, and yield-management equipment used by chipmakers.

nodes.label: ZEISS SMT, Oberkochen
nodes.whyItMatters: Oberkochen is ZEISS SMT's headquarters and production site for the lithography optics integrated into ASML systems.

nodes.label: Shin-Etsu Handotai, Shirakawa
nodes.whyItMatters: Shirakawa is a principal integrated production site for monocrystalline silicon, polished wafers, and epitaxial wafers.

nodes.label: SUMCO Imari-Nagahama
nodes.whyItMatters: SUMCO's Imari-Nagahama site designs and produces monocrystalline silicon products for semiconductor devices.

nodes.label: JSR Yokkaichi
nodes.whyItMatters: JSR's Yokkaichi plant hosts its Fine Electronic Materials Development Center for leading-edge photoresists.

nodes.label: Tokyo Ohka Kogyo, Koriyama
nodes.whyItMatters: Koriyama manufactures EUV, ArF, and KrF photoresists and is expanding advanced photoresist capacity.

flows.label: Veldhoven to Tainan tools flow
flows.plain-language meaning: ASML in Veldhoven supplies lithography systems used by Taiwan's leading-edge fabs.

flows.label: Veldhoven to Pyeongtaek tools flow
flows.plain-language meaning: Samsung's Pyeongtaek fabs depend on advanced lithography systems supplied by ASML.

flows.label: Tainan to Phoenix foundry expansion
flows.plain-language meaning: TSMC's Phoenix fabs extend its Taiwan-centered production network into the United States.

flows.label: Taiwan to Kumamoto manufacturing extension
flows.plain-language meaning: The Kumamoto fab extends a Taiwan-led foundry network into Japan.

flows.label: Oberkochen to Veldhoven lithography-optics supply
flows.plain-language meaning: ZEISS supplies the lithography optics integrated into ASML's advanced lithography systems.

caveats: Stale≤6mo: fab ramp status, product-node roadmaps, backend capacity additions, and export-control coverage can change quickly.
A simplified homepage map may wrongly imply a single linear chain; real semiconductor production depends on many parallel supplier, design, packaging, and equipment relationships.
Country-level color fills obscure how production is concentrated in a few sites.
sensitiveOrDisputedClassifications: Tool flows show upstream dependence, not transaction-by-transaction shipments.
Phoenix should not be depicted as evidence of U.S. independence from Taiwanese production concentration.
missingEvidence: Public company reports do not provide complete, current, customer-by-customer routing maps.
Exact cross-facility dependency varies by chip type, foundry node, packaging path, and export-control treatment.

scenes.publicLabel: Frontier-AI compute, chips, cloud, research, and governance infrastructure
scenes.oneSentencePurpose: Frontier AI depends on a linked stack of compute, advanced chips, cloud regions, research hubs, and governance institutions.
scenes.evidenceWindow: asOf 2026-07-14; uses company filings, cloud-region pages, official AI-governance documents, and public compute announcements

countryRoles.rationale: The U.S. concentrates major cloud capacity, frontier model firms, GPU design leadership, fab re-shoring efforts, and federal AI governance institutions.
Advanced-model development still depends materially on Taiwanese leading-edge manufacturing capacity even when the compute is physically elsewhere.
The Dutch lithography bottleneck remains foundational to frontier-AI chip supply because advanced fabs depend on ASML's manufacturing and export-control environment.
Samsung's AI-oriented HBM and memory roadmap makes South Korea central to frontier compute scaling.
The UAE is building out AI capital, compute, and research infrastructure through G42, Khazna, MBZUAI, MGX, and formal technology partnerships.
The UK's AI Security Institute gives Britain a notable governance and evaluation role in the frontier-AI ecosystem.

nodes.label: Northern Virginia cloud belt
nodes.whyItMatters: Northern Virginia is a major U.S. cloud region for hyperscale AI training and inference.

nodes.label: Santa Clara Bay Area AI hardware cluster
nodes.whyItMatters: Santa Clara concentrates frontier-AI hardware, software, and investment, including NVIDIA.

nodes.label: Washington, DC
nodes.whyItMatters: Washington sets federal AI standards and export policy.

nodes.label: Hsinchu-Tainan advanced fab axis
nodes.whyItMatters: The Hsinchu-Tainan corridor produces advanced chips used in frontier AI systems.

nodes.label: Pyeongtaek memory complex
nodes.whyItMatters: Pyeongtaek produces high-bandwidth and server memory used in AI systems.

nodes.label: ASML Veldhoven
nodes.whyItMatters: Veldhoven supplies lithography equipment required to make frontier-AI chips.

nodes.label: Abu Dhabi AI campus and research cluster
nodes.whyItMatters: Abu Dhabi combines capital, compute, sovereign-cloud ambition, and MBZUAI-led research in one increasingly visible node.

nodes.label: London AI governance node
nodes.whyItMatters: London hosts the UK AI Security Institute, a major center for AI evaluation and governance.

flows.label: Veldhoven to Taiwan fab bottleneck flow
flows.plain-language meaning: Advanced lithography from Veldhoven supports frontier-chip production in Taiwan.

flows.label: Taiwan fabs to U.S. cloud compute
flows.plain-language meaning: U.S. cloud infrastructure depends on advanced chips made in Taiwan.

flows.label: Bay Area hardware-design ecosystem to cloud deployment
flows.plain-language meaning: NVIDIA hardware designed in the Bay Area is deployed across U.S. hyperscale cloud infrastructure.

flows.label: Abu Dhabi capital and compute partnership with U.S. stack
flows.plain-language meaning: UAE capital and infrastructure partnerships connect Abu Dhabi to Microsoft and other U.S.-linked AI projects.

flows.label: Washington-London AI safety and standards channel
flows.plain-language meaning: U.S. and UK AI safety institutes coordinate on model evaluation and international standards.

caveats: Stale≤6mo: compute-capacity announcements, data-center buildouts, AI-campus timelines, cloud-region capacity claims, and governance implementation calendars can change very quickly.
A simplified homepage map may falsely imply that training compute, inference compute, fab output, memory supply, and governance institutions move at the same pace; they do not.
The flow lines represent infrastructure dependencies. They do not represent published shipment routes.
sensitiveOrDisputedClassifications: Taiwan's role in frontier-AI chip supply is undeniable in public sources, but any map should avoid implying diplomatic recognition from technical dependence.
Abu Dhabi's AI-campus and finance role is growing fast; editorial treatment should not assume announced projects are already fully delivered.
missingEvidence: Public sources do not disclose full procurement relationships, utilization rates, or model-by-model training footprints.
Cloud-region pages identify geography and capacity categories better than they reveal frontier-model-specific deployment.
